text:
alex: pushed a Grafana dashboard for GPU per-MIG-slice metrics + token-latency waterfall. panels: SM occupancy by slice, VRAM per process, power/thermal, token latency waterfall broken into decode / kv_lookup / kernel_exec. also per-route KPIs (route=chat/embed/rerank) and kernel selection tags. feedback? <http://grafana.local/d/XyZ/perf-mig-token-waterfall>

maria: nice. saw a consistent spike on slice-3 after the last kernel-selector change. can we map that to a specific kernel_id?

alex: yes — runtime now emits `kernel_id` label. example query I added: `histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(token_latency_bucket{kernel!=""}[5m])) by (route,kernel_id)`

simon: kv cache miss rate seems elevated for short prefixes. I see `kv_prefetch_enabled=0` on the host that hit the spike. could be why decode time + kernel exec both jumped.

infra-bot: deploy bot: rolled out commit r/serve@ae3f2 to prod at 1776400100

priya: repro steps I used: small load with `seq=256 batch_strategy=latency` and watched `sm_efficiency` drop to ~42%. nvprof/cupti snapshot shows heavy L2 thrash during the fallback kernel.

matt: can we add tensor core util and L2 hit ratio panels? those narrow down kernel inefficiencies quickly.

alex: added panels for `tensor_core_utilization` and `l2_cache_hit_ratio`. also added a short log panel that surfaces kernel selector decisions, example line:
```
2026-03-18T10:02:45Z kernel_select: model=redwood-v2 variant=fp16 seq_len=256 selected=kernel_v3 fallback_reason="no_tensor_cores"
```

maria: should we annotate the dashboard with recent commits and perf-rollback window? that would make chasing regressions easier.

simon: also seeing two containers accidentally colocated on the same MIG slice under high load — MIG contention shows as sm_efficiency drop + increased pcie stall. scheduler probably needs isolation rules for latency-sensitive routes.

alex: proposal: add autoscheduler policy that avoids colocating routes with SLA="low-latency" on same MIG slice; opened a draft PR (link in thread).

priya: another data point: KV cache TTL is per-session now. for high-churn chat routes we should consider per-route TTL or adaptive TTL based on prefix hit rate.

matt: one small nit — token panels use `rate(...[5m])` which smooths short spikes. for token-level SLO alerts use `1m` windows so we catch brief regressions.

alex: good call, changed some panels to `1m` and added alert: `alert if p95 token_decode > 200ms for route=chat for 2m` using `avg_over_time(token_decode_p95{route="chat"}[2m]) > 0.2`

maria: can we add a breakdown panel that shows contribution per stage (kv_lookup, kernel_exec, postprocess) as stacked bars? helps in postmortems.

alex: added stacked breakdown and a per-route scatter for `kernel_exec_ms vs batch_size` so we can tune batching heuristics. sample query for KV miss ratio by route: `sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[1m])) by (route) / sum(rate(kv_cache_lookup_total[1m])) by (route)`

simon: thanks — will run a focused load test tomorrow with `batch_strategy=throughput` and `seq=128/512` combos and post results here.

priya: heads up — I'll attach CUPTI flamegraphs and the nv-host logs after the run.

matt: LGTM. when infra-bot rolled r/serve@ae3f2 did we also change default `kernel_prefer_tensor_cores`? that could explain fallback behavior.

alex: yes, the change toggled prefer flag for some model variants. I'll gate that behind a canary for the next rollout.

maria: :thumbsup: this dashboard looks great. fine-grained metrics + kernel_id label make root-cause much faster.

alex: thanks all — will iterate on panels/alerts based on the test results. filing follow-ups: autoscheduler isolation + KV TTL per-route + canary revert rule.
